question.text: A DDQ from an Indian SWF asks: 'Describe your Key-Man Clause and its consequences.' Per Ch 12, upon a Key-Man event, the STANDARD investor protection is:

answer.text: Automatic dissolution of the fund within 30 days, with pro-rata distribution at cost.
Suspension of new investments and investors typically request compulsory redemption/exit without charges unless a suitable replacement is found within pre-agreed timelines and informed to SEBI.
The fund must be transferred to an alternate Manager chosen by SEBI.
The Sponsor automatically buys out all LP interests at the last NAV.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 12: Key-Man clause prohibits new investments until replacement is arranged. Investors 'ask for a compulsory redemption/exit without charges in case of a key man event unless a suitable replacement is found within pre-agreed timelines and informed to SEBI'. **The Trap:** A, C, D are fabricated extreme outcomes. SEBI does not choose replacements; Manager does, LP advisory board consents. **Cross-Exam Context:** Key-Person clause is a core GP/LP negotiation point — similar conceptually to force-majeure in project finance. In XXI-B (PM) there is no equivalent — the PM can be replaced by client without such cliff-trigger. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Pre-negotiate a 60-day 'cure period' in the LPA: if a super-key leaves, you have 60 days to propose a replacement, subject to LP Advisory Board approval. This protects both sides vs an instant suspension.
